finding.title: Make AppUser/AuthState/AuthUser @freezed instead of hand-rolled classes without value equality
finding.why: AppUser, AuthState and AuthUser are plain hand-written classes (immutable, but no @freezed, no custom ==/hashCode), so two instances with identical field values compare unequal by reference identity — AuthState is literally the `state` type of a keepAlive Riverpod Notifier. Current consumers avoid the fallout by exclusively `.select()`-ing down to primitive sub-fields (e.g. `s.currentUser?.firebaseUid`, a String, in manage_tutors_providers.dart/app_shell.dart/persistent_switcher_scaffold.dart) rather than comparing whole AuthState values, so no concrete rebuild-storm is demonstrated today — but it is a landmine for the next `ref.watch(authStateProvider)` call that doesn't remember to add a `.select()`.
finding.recommendation: Convert to @freezed (or at minimum implement value ==/hashCode) — low-risk given the classes are small and already immutable.
acceptance_criteria: AuthState(...) == AuthState(...) is true for equal field values (documents the fix via a unit test)
build_runner regenerates cleanly with no call-site breakage

finding.title: Extract a shared pumpApp test helper — profiles feature hand-rolls the 4-delegate MaterialApp wrapper 13 times
finding.why: TQ-3 calls for widget tests to pump via a shared pumpApp helper; test/helpers/ has no such file (verified contents: drift_memory.dart, firestore_fake.dart, golden_runner.dart, migration_test_helper.dart, overflow_harness.dart, test_database.dart). Each of the 4 widget-test files in this batch hand-rolls the identical MaterialApp+localizationsDelegates+supportedLocales block (6 separate occurrences inside pin_flow_and_setup_dialog_l1_test.dart alone; 13 total in this batch), and the same block appears in 146 test files repo-wide (grepped for GlobalCupertinoLocalizations.delegate). Any future change to the delegate list, theme, or a required test-only ancestor widget requires hand-editing every copy; a missed copy silently diverges from the rest.
finding.recommendation: Add test/helpers/pump_app.dart exposing a pumpApp({child, overrides, locale}) helper and migrate these call sites onto it, starting with this batch's 4 files.
acceptance_criteria: test/helpers/pump_app.dart exists and is used by at least the 4 files in this batch
A tracked grep count of GlobalCupertinoLocalizations.delegate outside test/helpers/ decreases as files migrate

finding.title: Add profileId to TrackLearningOrder — the one user_database table with a bare autoincrement PK, and make audit's claimed profileId check doesn't exist

evidence.quote:
final insertable = TrackLearningOrderCompanion.custom(
        trackId: const Variable(1),
**Enforcement:** `make audit` flags any user-DB table without a `profileId` column.

finding.why: Both test files in this batch construct TrackLearningOrderCompanion.insert()/.custom() with only trackId/sefariaRef/sortOrder — never profileId — because lib/core/database/tables/track_learning_order.dart has no profileId column at all (confirmed by direct read: bare autoIncrement `id`, only trackId + sefariaRef + sortOrder, uniqueKeys is {trackId, sefariaRef}). Every sibling user-data table in the batch's test evidence (bookmarks, goals, daily_plans, learning_order, streak_events, completion_events, stage_definitions, ...) carries an explicit profileId. Isolation for this table depends entirely on trackId never being confused across profiles; a caching or profile-switch bug elsewhere that reuses a stale trackId would silently read/write another profile's (e.g. a sibling child's) custom text ordering with no schema-level guard to catch it. This gap is currently invisible: `grep -n profileId learning_tracker/Makefile` returns zero matches, so none of the 22 `make audit` checks actually implements the check the standards doc says exists — the rule is marked [E] (Enforced) but enforces nothing for this table.
finding.recommendation: Add a profileId IntColumn (FK to learner_profiles, cascade delete) to TrackLearningOrder, fold it into the uniqueKeys constraint with trackId/sefariaRef, ship it as a schemaVersion bump per DB-4 discipline (migration step + schema export + migration test), and update the DAO. Separately, write the actual `make audit` grep the doc already claims exists so this class of gap is caught mechanically going forward.
acceptance_criteria: lib/core/database/tables/track_learning_order.dart has a profileId column referencing learner_profiles, with a migration step and committed schema export at the new schemaVersion.

A `make audit` check greps every table in lib/core/database/tables/*.dart used by UserDatabase and fails if profileId is absent (unless the table is on a documented content-table exemption list), closing the doc/reality gap at docs/coding-standards.md:689.

finding.title: Rewrite completion_dao_test.dart null-scope test — the null-check operator throws before the DAO method is ever called

evidence.quote: test('getAllCompletions throws AssertionError in debug when scope is null '

finding.why: Dart evaluates argument expressions before invoking the function, so `scope: nullableScope!` throws TypeError the instant the null-check operator runs — internalGetAllCompletionsCrossProfile (and any internal _assertCrossProfileScope guard inside it) is never entered. The test's own docstring claims it 'verifies the assert fires in debug mode,' but it actually only verifies core Dart null-safety semantics, unrelated to any code in completion_dao.dart. If the DAO's internal scope guard were deleted entirely, this test would still pass unchanged, so it provides zero regression coverage for the behavior it claims to protect.
finding.recommendation: Delete this test (Dart's null-safety already makes a null CrossProfileScope unreachable through the typed public API, so there is nothing left to regress) or rewrite it to genuinely exercise the DAO's internal guard via a testable seam.
acceptance_criteria: Test either removed with a comment explaining the language-level reason, or rewritten so it demonstrably enters completion_dao.dart code before throwing
No remaining test claims to verify an internal assert that it cannot actually reach

finding.title: Close every inMemoryDb() Drift database opened by tracks/setup and track_order widget tests
finding.rule: TQ-6 (hermetic tests / no shared/leaked state) — violates drift_memory.dart's own documented contract

evidence.quote:
/// Callers MUST `await db.close()` in `tearDown` to free the native
/// resources.

finding.why: drift_memory.dart's own doc comment says callers MUST close every inMemoryDb() in tearDown to free native FFI/sqlite3 resources. step_starting_position_l1_test.dart creates 6 in-memory DBs (lines 222, 234, 251, 1017, 1075, 1127) and closes none. track_management_body_and_order_l1_test.dart creates 8 and closes only 3 (the other 5 — lines 158, 204, 304, 461, 929 — leak once per test invocation that hits them, i.e. ~13+ leaked native handles across that file's test run). track_management_hub_screen_l1_test.dart's shared default at line 120 leaks once per test that doesn't pass an explicit db (~10 tests). track_learning_order_reset_test.dart's single DB is never closed. Across a full CI run this accumulates open native sqlite3 handles per test file, risking slow teardown/fd pressure and contradicts the helper's explicit contract.
finding.recommendation: Add `addTearDown(() => database.close())` (or an explicit `await db.close()`) immediately after every inMemoryDb() call site listed, including the shared `db ?? inMemoryDb()` defaults in _buildBodyApp/_buildApp/_buildStartingPositionApp-style helpers.
acceptance_criteria: Every inMemoryDb() call in the 4 listed files is paired with a db.close() (or addTearDown close) reachable on both pass and fail paths
A Rule-0 grep/lint (e.g. compare inMemoryDb() count vs close()/addTearDown-close count per test file) fails CI when the counts diverge
